nodes.label: README-First Analysis Strategy
nodes.rationale: Documentation is inspected before the full codebase to reduce analysis time and context usage while identifying project purpose, features, and startup instructions.

nodes.label: Lead Hunter Modular Architecture
nodes.rationale: Responsibilities are separated across the main entry point and specialized scraper, auditor, exporter, GUI, and configuration modules.

nodes.label: Fail-Fast Centralized API Configuration
nodes.rationale: Centralized fail-fast API-key handling is identified as a robustness strength of the project.

nodes.label: Enterprise-ready B2B Sales Intelligence Claim
nodes.rationale: The README positions the application as enterprise-ready because it combines geofenced discovery, crawling, LLM auditing and export into one automated pipeline.

nodes.label: External Service and Pipeline Configuration
nodes.rationale: Centralized constants govern Google Places, geocoding, OpenRouter models, geographic coverage, filtering thresholds, crawler limits and output paths.

nodes.label: Crawl4AI Semantic Crawling
nodes.rationale: The synchronized implementation replaces the former custom static/Playwright crawler with Crawl4AI to produce semantic Markdown, structured links and browser-backed rendering.

nodes.label: No-website Lead Discovery Pipeline
nodes.rationale: This mode discovers and deduplicates businesses without a website, but currently returns raw Places data without invoking the available AI audit method.

nodes.label: Website Opportunity Audit Pipeline
nodes.rationale: This mode chains Places discovery, qualification filters, site crawling, email extraction, LLM audit and spreadsheet export to produce sales opportunities.
